content.json: # Microsoft Defender for Office 365 - Mail Anomalies

## MDO Mail Anomalies
This workbook shows mail-borne attack patterns tracked by Microsoft Threat Intelligence and surfaced by **Microsoft Defender for Office 365**. Use the tabs to drill into each anomaly. Companion **Defender XDR custom detections** are in the `CustomDetections` folder of [homelabber/MDO-Anomalies](https://github.com/homelabber/MDO-Anomalies).

**Data sources:** EmailEvents, EmailUrlInfo, EmailAttachmentInfo, EmailPostDeliveryEvents, UrlClickEvents and CloudAppEvents (Microsoft Defender XDR connector), SigninLogs (Entra ID connector), plus MessageEvents, DeviceProcessEvents and IdentityInfo where available. Streaming records are deduplicated per NetworkMessageId + recipient.

content.query:
let Email = EmailEvents
| where TimeGenerated {TimeRange}
| summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, *) by NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress;
let Clicks = UrlClickEvents | where TimeGenerated {TimeRange};
union isfuzzy=true
(Email | where EmailDirection == "Inbound" and DetectionMethods has "Mail bombing" | summarize Value = dcount(RecipientEmailAddress) | extend Anomaly = "01 Email bombing", Unit = "users targeted"),
(Email | join kind=inner (EmailUrlInfo | where TimeGenerated {TimeRange} | where UrlLocation == "QRCode" | distinct NetworkMessageId) on NetworkMessageId | summarize Value = dcount(NetworkMessageId) | extend Anomaly = "03 QR code mail", Unit = "messages"),
(Email | where EmailDirection == "Inbound" and SenderFromDomain =~ RecipientDomain | extend A = parse_json(AuthenticationDetails) | where DetectionMethods has "Spoof intra-org" or (isempty(Connectors) and tostring(A.SPF) !~ "pass" and tostring(A.DMARC) !in~ ("pass", "bestguesspass")) | summarize Value = count() | extend Anomaly = "04 Direct Send / intra-org spoof", Unit = "messages"),
(EmailAttachmentInfo | where TimeGenerated {TimeRange} | where FileName matches regex @"(?i)\.(svgz?|s?html?|xhtml|mhtml?)$" | summarize Value = dcount(NetworkMessageId) | extend Anomaly = "05 HTML/SVG attachments", Unit = "messages"),
(Clicks | where ThreatTypes has "Phish" and (ActionType == "ClickAllowed" or tostring(IsClickedThrough) in ("1", "true", "True")) | summarize Value = dcount(AccountUpn) | extend Anomaly = "06 Phish clicks allowed", Unit = "users"),
(Clicks | where UrlChain has_any ("microsoft.com/devicelogin", "oauth2/deviceauth") | summarize Value = dcount(AccountUpn) | extend Anomaly = "07 Device-login URL clicks", Unit = "users"),
(Email | where EmailDirection == "Inbound" and DetectionMethods has "Impersonation" | summarize Value = count() | extend Anomaly = "08 Impersonation", Unit = "messages"),
(Email | where EmailDirection == "Inbound" and ThreatTypes has "Phish" and UrlCount == 0 | summarize Value = count() | extend Anomaly = "09 URL-less phish (callback)", Unit = "messages"),
(Email | where EmailDirection == "Outbound" and (isnotempty(ThreatTypes) or DeliveryAction == "Blocked") | summarize Value = dcount(SenderFromAddress) | extend Anomaly = "10 Outbound flagged senders", Unit = "senders"),
(EmailPostDeliveryEvents | where TimeGenerated {TimeRange} | where ActionType has "ZAP" and ActionResult !~ "Success" | summarize Value = count() | extend Anomaly = "11 Failed ZAP actions", Unit = "actions"),
(CloudAppEvents | where TimeGenerated {TimeRange} | where ActionType in ("New-InboxRule", "Set-InboxRule", "UpdateInboxRules") | summarize Value = count() | extend Anomaly = "12 Inbox rule changes", Unit = "events"),
(Email | where EmailDirection == "Inbound" and DetectionMethods has "LLM content analysis" | summarize Value = count() | extend Anomaly = "14 LLM content analysis", Unit = "messages")
| order by Anomaly asc
content.title: Anomaly summary
content.noDataMessage: No matching activity in the selected time range.

content.json:
### Email bombing
The attacker subscribes the victim to hundreds of newsletters and sign-up forms to bury real alerts. Storm-1811 and Black Basta affiliates use it as the opener for fake help-desk calls. MDO tags this mail with the **Mail bombing** detection technology.

**Custom detection:** `MDO-01`

content.title: Mail-bombing tagged messages per recipient
content.noDataMessage: No matching activity in the selected time range.

content.query:
let Email = EmailEvents
| where TimeGenerated {TimeRange}
| summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, *) by NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress;
Email
| where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
| summarize Total = count(), MailBombingTagged = countif(DetectionMethods has "Mail bombing"), DistinctSenderDomains = dcount(SenderFromDomain),
    DeliveredToInbox = countif(DeliveryLocation == "Inbox/folder"), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated),
    SampleSubjects = make_set(Subject, 5) by RecipientEmailAddress, Hour = bin(TimeGenerated, 1h)
| where MailBombingTagged > 0 or (Total >= 100 and DistinctSenderDomains >= 20)
| order by MailBombingTagged desc, Total desc
content.title: Recipients under email bombing
content.noDataMessage: No matching activity in the selected time range.

content.json:
### Email bombing followed by external Teams contact or remote-access tool
After the flood, the actor calls the victim or messages them from an **external Teams tenant** as "IT support" and talks them into running **Quick Assist** or another RMM tool. This tab joins bombed users to external Teams chats (MessageEvents) and remote-tool launches (DeviceProcessEvents) within 24 hours.

**Custom detections:** `MDO-02a`, `MDO-02b`. Reference: [Threat actors misusing Quick Assist](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2024/05/15/threat-actors-misusing-quick-assist-in-social-engineering-attacks-leading-to-ransomware/)

content.query:
let Email = EmailEvents
| where TimeGenerated {TimeRange}
| summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, *) by NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress;
let Bombed = Email
| where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
| summarize Total = count(), Tagged = countif(DetectionMethods has "Mail bombing"), Domains = dcount(SenderFromDomain), BombStart = min(TimeGenerated) by Recipient = tolower(RecipientEmailAddress)
| where Tagged >= 10 or (Total >= 100 and Domains >= 20);
let RemoteTools = dynamic(["quickassist.exe","anydesk.exe","teamviewer.exe","screenconnect.clientservice.exe","screenconnect.windowsclient.exe","rustdesk.exe","splashtop.exe","srservice.exe","zaservice.exe","rutserv.exe","supremo.exe","client32.exe","atera_agent.exe","dwagent.exe"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(MessageEvents
    | where TimeGenerated {TimeRange}
    | where IsExternalThread == true
    | mv-expand R = RecipientDetails
    | extend Recipient = tolower(tostring(R.RecipientSmtpAddress))
    | project TimeGenerated, Recipient, Signal = "External Teams message", Detail = strcat(SenderDisplayName, " <", SenderEmailAddress, ">")),
(DeviceProcessEvents
    | where TimeGenerated {TimeRange}
    | where FileName in~ (RemoteTools)
    | extend Recipient = tolower(coalesce(AccountUpn, InitiatingProcessAccountUpn))
    | project TimeGenerated, Recipient, Signal = "Remote tool launched", Detail = strcat(FileName, " on ", DeviceName)),
(datatable(TimeGenerated: datetime, Recipient: string, Signal: string, Detail: string)[])
| join kind=inner Bombed on Recipient
| where TimeGenerated between (BombStart .. (BombStart + 24h))
| project TimeGenerated, Recipient, Signal, Detail, BombStart, BombMessages = Total, MailBombingTagged = Tagged
| order by TimeGenerated desc
content.title: Bombed users with follow-up Teams contact or remote-tool launch
content.noDataMessage: No matching activity in the selected time range.

content.query:

### QR code phishing (quishing)
QR codes move the phishing URL to an unmanaged phone, out of reach of Safe Links. MDO extracts QR URLs and records them in EmailUrlInfo with `UrlLocation == "QRCode"`.

**Custom detection:** `MDO-03`

| summarize QrUrls = make_set(Url, 5), QrDomains = make_set(UrlDomain, 5) by NetworkMessageId;
QR | mv-expand QrDomains to typeof(string)
| summarize Messages = count() by QrDomains | top 15 by Messages

content.json:
### Direct Send / internal-domain spoofing
Exchange Online **Direct Send** accepts unauthenticated mail to your MX for your own accepted domains. Attackers abuse it to send messages that appear internal (voicemail, HR, invoices). If you don't need Direct Send, consider `Set-OrganizationConfig -RejectDirectSend $true`.

**Custom detection:** `MDO-04`

content.title: Spoofed internal-domain mail by outcome
content.noDataMessage: No matching activity in the selected time range.

content.query:
let Email = EmailEvents
| where TimeGenerated {TimeRange}
| summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, *) by NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress;
let DirectSend = Email
| where EmailDirection == "Inbound" and SenderFromDomain =~ RecipientDomain
| extend A = parse_json(AuthenticationDetails)
| extend SPF = tostring(A.SPF), DKIM = tostring(A.DKIM), DMARC = tostring(A.DMARC), CompAuth = tostring(A.CompAuth)
| where DetectionMethods has "Spoof intra-org" or (isempty(Connectors) and SPF !~ "pass" and DMARC !in~ ("pass", "bestguesspass"));
DirectSend
| project TimeGenerated, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress, SenderMailFromDomain, SenderIPv4, Subject, DeliveryAction, DeliveryLocation, SPF, DKIM, DMARC, CompAuth, DetectionMethods
| order by TimeGenerated desc

SVG images and HTML files can carry JavaScript that builds a credential-phishing page or drops a payload locally, so it never touches URL scanning. Consider blocking these types with the common attachments filter.

content.json:
### Adversary-in-the-middle (AiTM) phishing
AiTM kits (for example Tycoon2FA and EvilProxy) proxy the real Microsoft sign-in page and steal the session cookie. This tab correlates allowed or clicked-through phishing URLs with successful Entra ID sign-ins from a different IP within 1 hour.

**Custom detection:** `MDO-06`

content.query:
UrlClickEvents
| where TimeGenerated {TimeRange}
| where ThreatTypes has "Phish" and (ActionType == "ClickAllowed" or tostring(IsClickedThrough) in ("1", "true", "True"))
| project TimeGenerated, AccountUpn, Url, ActionType, IsClickedThrough, Workload, IPAddress, NetworkMessageId
| order by TimeGenerated desc
content.title: Phishing URL clicks that were allowed or clicked through
content.noDataMessage: No matching activity in the selected time range.

content.query:
let Clicks = UrlClickEvents
| where TimeGenerated {TimeRange}
| where (ThreatTypes has "Phish" and ActionType == "ClickAllowed") or tostring(IsClickedThrough) in ("1", "true", "True")
| project ClickTime = TimeGenerated, User = tolower(AccountUpn), ClickIP = IPAddress, Url;
SigninLogs
| where TimeGenerated {TimeRange}
| where ResultType == "0"
| extend User = tolower(UserPrincipalName)
| join kind=inner Clicks on User
| where TimeGenerated between (ClickTime .. (ClickTime + 1h)) and IPAddress != ClickIP
| project SignInTime = TimeGenerated, User, ClickTime, Url, ClickIP, SignInIP = IPAddress, Location, AppDisplayName, RiskLevelDuringSignIn, UserAgent
| order by SignInTime desc
content.title: Clicks followed by a successful sign-in from a different IP (1 hour)
content.noDataMessage: No matching activity in the selected time range.

content.json:
### Device code phishing
The actor (for example Storm-2372) sends a lure (a Teams meeting invite, document, or chat) that asks the user to enter a code at `microsoft.com/devicelogin`, which hands the actor the user's tokens. Consider a Conditional Access policy that blocks the device code flow for users who don't need it.

**Custom detection:** `MDO-07`. Reference: [Storm-2372 device code phishing](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2025/02/13/storm-2372-conducts-device-code-phishing-campaign/)

content.query:
SigninLogs
| where TimeGenerated {TimeRange}
| where AuthenticationProtocol == "deviceCode"
| summarize count() by ResultType, bin(TimeGenerated, {TimeRange:grain})
content.title: Device code sign-ins over time
content.noDataMessage: No matching activity in the selected time range.

content.title: Mail containing device-login URLs
content.noDataMessage: No matching activity in the selected time range.

content.query:
let Clicks = UrlClickEvents
| where TimeGenerated {TimeRange}
| where UrlChain has_any ("microsoft.com/devicelogin", "oauth2/deviceauth", "aka.ms/devicelogin")
| summarize LastClick = max(TimeGenerated) by User = tolower(AccountUpn);
SigninLogs
| where TimeGenerated {TimeRange}
| where AuthenticationProtocol == "deviceCode"
| extend User = tolower(UserPrincipalName)
| join kind=leftouter Clicks on User
| extend PrecededByClick = isnotempty(LastClick) and TimeGenerated between (LastClick - 2m .. LastClick + 30m)
| project TimeGenerated, User, ResultType, AppDisplayName, IPAddress, Location, RiskLevelDuringSignIn, PrecededByClick
| order by PrecededByClick desc, TimeGenerated desc
content.title: Device code sign-ins (flag: preceded by device-login URL click)
content.noDataMessage: No matching activity in the selected time range.

content.json:
### Callback phishing (TOAD: telephone-oriented attack delivery)
These lures contain **no links**, just a fake invoice or subscription renewal and a phone number. The phone call leads to remote-access installs or payment fraud. Because the message body isn't in the tables, this tab uses URL-less phish verdicts and billing-themed mail from free-mail senders. **Workbook only** (no custom detection) because of the false-positive rate.

content.json:
### Compromised account sending outbound spam/phish
Compromised mailboxes are used to phish partners and coworkers. Look for senders whose outbound mail is being flagged or blocked, or whose volume spikes. Also check the **Restricted entities** page in the Defender portal.

**Custom detection:** `MDO-10`

content.title: Outbound volume - top 10 senders
content.noDataMessage: No matching activity in the selected time range.

content.query:
let Email = EmailEvents
| where TimeGenerated {TimeRange}
| summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, *) by NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress;
Email
| where EmailDirection == "Outbound"
| summarize Total = count(), Flagged = countif(isnotempty(ThreatTypes) or DeliveryAction in ("Blocked", "Junked")), Recipients = dcount(RecipientEmailAddress),
    RecipientDomains = dcount(RecipientDomain), ThreatTypes = make_set(ThreatTypes, 5), SampleSubjects = make_set(Subject, 5) by SenderFromAddress
| where Flagged > 0
| extend FlaggedPct = round(100.0 * Flagged / Total, 1)
| order by Flagged desc
content.title: Outbound senders with flagged or blocked mail

content.json:
### Malicious mail still in inboxes (ZAP missed or failed)
Zero-hour auto purge (ZAP) removes mail that is found malicious after delivery. ZAP failures, allow-list overrides, or a disabled ZAP policy can leave phish or malware in the inbox. (LatestDeliveryLocation isn't streamed to Sentinel, so this tab uses EmailPostDeliveryEvents. The custom detection uses LatestDeliveryLocation directly.)

**Custom detection:** `MDO-11`

content.title: Post-delivery actions by result

EmailPostDeliveryEvents
| where TimeGenerated {TimeRange}
| where ActionResult !~ "Success"
| project TimeGenerated, RecipientEmailAddress, ActionType, Action, ActionTrigger, ActionResult, ThreatTypes, DeliveryLocation, NetworkMessageId

content.json:
### Inbox and forwarding rules after phishing
After an account takeover, actors create rules that delete or hide replies (often moving them to RSS or Archive) or that forward mail out. This tab flags rule changes by users who received phish or clicked a phishing URL in the previous 3 days.

**Custom detection:** `MDO-12`

content.query:
let Email = EmailEvents
| where TimeGenerated {TimeRange}
| summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, *) by NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress;
let Exposed = union
    (Email | where EmailDirection == "Inbound" and DeliveryAction == "Delivered" and ThreatTypes has "Phish" | project T = TimeGenerated, User = tolower(RecipientEmailAddress)),
    (UrlClickEvents | where TimeGenerated {TimeRange} | where ThreatTypes has "Phish" | project T = TimeGenerated, User = tolower(AccountUpn))
| summarize FirstExposure = min(T) by User;
CloudAppEvents
| where TimeGenerated {TimeRange}
| where ActionType in ("New-InboxRule", "Set-InboxRule", "UpdateInboxRules", "Set-Mailbox")
| extend Params = tostring(RawEventData.Parameters), User = tolower(tostring(RawEventData.UserId))
| where ActionType != "Set-Mailbox" or Params has_any ("ForwardingSmtpAddress", "ForwardingAddress", "DeliverToMailboxAndForward")
| where Params has_any ("DeleteMessage", "MoveToFolder", "MarkAsRead", "ForwardTo", "RedirectTo", "ForwardAsAttachmentTo", "ForwardingSmtpAddress", "ForwardingAddress", "RSS", "Archive", "Conversation History")
| join kind=leftouter Exposed on User
| extend AfterPhishExposure = isnotempty(FirstExposure) and TimeGenerated between (FirstExposure .. (FirstExposure + 3d))
| project TimeGenerated, User, ActionType, AfterPhishExposure, FirstExposure, IPAddress, CountryCode, Params
| order by AfterPhishExposure desc, TimeGenerated desc
content.title: Suspicious inbox/forwarding rule changes
content.noDataMessage: No matching activity in the selected time range.

content.json:
### Look-alike and newly seen sender domains
BEC and phishing campaigns often use typosquatted versions of your domain (for example `contos0.com` or `contoso-support.com`) or freshly registered domains. This tab normalizes common character swaps (rn to m, 0 to o, 1 to l, vv to w) and compares sender domains with your recipient domains. It also lists sender domains not seen in the prior 30 days. **Workbook only.**

content.json:
### Mail flagged by MDO's LLM content analysis
Defender for Office 365 runs purpose-built large language models that read the message's content and **intent** (for example urgency, payment-change requests, credential requests, or callback lures). Matches show up as the **LLM content analysis** detection technology.

**How to read this tab:** this is mail that *Microsoft's* AI flagged. It does **not** prove the attacker used AI to write it, and nothing in the data shows that. **LLM-only** detections, where no reputation, detonation, impersonation, or fingerprint signal also fired, are the best available stand-in for novel, well-written lures (often AI-assisted) that traditional filters would have missed. Workbook only.

content.query:
let Email = EmailEvents
| where TimeGenerated {TimeRange}
| summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, *) by NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress;
let LLM = Email
| where EmailDirection == "Inbound" and DetectionMethods has "LLM content analysis"
| extend DM = parse_json(DetectionMethods)
| mv-expand Threat = bag_keys(DM) to typeof(string)
| mv-expand Tech = DM[Threat] to typeof(string)
| summarize Techs = make_set(Tech), Threats = make_set(Threat),
    take_any(TimeGenerated, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, Subject, DeliveryAction, DeliveryLocation, UrlCount, AttachmentCount, EmailDirection)
    by NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress
| extend OtherTechs = set_difference(Techs, dynamic(["LLM content analysis"]))
| extend LlmOnly = array_length(OtherTechs) == 0;
LLM | mv-expand Threat = Threats to typeof(string)
| summarize count() by Threat, bin(TimeGenerated, {TimeRange:grain})
content.title: LLM-flagged messages by threat type
content.noDataMessage: No matching activity in the selected time range.

content.query:
let Email = EmailEvents
| where TimeGenerated {TimeRange}
| summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, *) by NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress;
let LLM = Email
| where EmailDirection == "Inbound" and DetectionMethods has "LLM content analysis"
| extend DM = parse_json(DetectionMethods)
| mv-expand Threat = bag_keys(DM) to typeof(string)
| mv-expand Tech = DM[Threat] to typeof(string)
| summarize Techs = make_set(Tech), Threats = make_set(Threat),
    take_any(TimeGenerated, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, Subject, DeliveryAction, DeliveryLocation, UrlCount, AttachmentCount, EmailDirection)
    by NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress
| extend OtherTechs = set_difference(Techs, dynamic(["LLM content analysis"]))
| extend LlmOnly = array_length(OtherTechs) == 0;
LLM
| project TimeGenerated, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress, Subject, Threats, LlmOnly, OtherTechs, UrlCount, AttachmentCount, DeliveryAction, DeliveryLocation
| order by LlmOnly desc, TimeGenerated desc
content.title: LLM-flagged messages
content.noDataMessage: No matching activity in the selected time range.
